reviews.text: It's certainly pleasurable, but this modern Fatal Attraction is too prudish to satisfy.
reviews.author: Christina Newland

reviews.text: Around halfway through, as the ambiguity of the early scenes is lost, and we get a clearer sense of what exactly is happening, Deep Water also becomes more predictable, and refuses to gather steam as a thriller.
reviews.author: Jai Arjun Singh

reviews.text: Even if these types of thrillers are your guilty pleasure, no matter how bad or predictable they may be, forcing yourself through two hours of lifeless and uninspired writing and performances of this sort is simply not worth it.
reviews.author: Yasmine Kandil

reviews.text: “Deep Water” can be a bit shallow and silly at times. But the basic thrills and surprising laughs it provides are more than enough to make for an entertaining evening.
reviews.author: Kevin Slane

reviews.text: After watching this film I am trying to comprehend how the two leads fell in love while filming.
reviews.author: Jillian Chilingerian

reviews.text: One of the most frustrating & Boring films that I have seen in awhile. Yes there is some entertainment to it… but it goes away so fast & the film is only saved by the performances.
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: The protagonists couldn't be more awful people in an incredibly toxic relationship that's frustrating to watch, but their lack of development and inexistent arcs make the narrative feel repetitive, predictable, and lacking intensity.
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: Enticing and twisted, Deep Water sucks us into the journey with mesmerising lead performances and the prospect of an exciting climax, but unfortunately when the final destination is reached, it almost doesn't seem worth it.
reviews.author: Rebecca Johnson

reviews.text: At the end of the day, it’s hard to call Deep Water disappointing. On the scale of the erotic thrillers that came before, it’s nothing memorable, but there is something admirable about its existence in 2022.
reviews.author: Tina Kakadelis

reviews.text: DEEP WATER is a well-made and enjoyable film. I laughed all the way through but it was mainly because of the direction of the story and where the sympathy for the characters lies.
reviews.author: Dolores Quintana

reviews.text: Deep Water has some very interesting ideas and some great performances from Ben Affleck and Ana de Armas but the story is very messy and convoluted at times. Times were it feels like the stacks are high and others where I questioned the point of the story
reviews.author: Samuel Leggett Jr.

reviews.text: It's surprisingly earnest in the film's tawdry convictions. Still, I can't quite recommend Deep Water as the movie gets in way over its head.
reviews.author: Eric Marchen

reviews.text: The result is an affair as dull and lifeless as one of the ex-lovers’ corpses floating in a river... if Indecent Proposal‘s Robert Redford walks up and offers you $1 million for one viewing of Deep Water, politely decline. It is simply not worth it.
reviews.author: Dallas King

reviews.text: There is an alluring quality to its trashy story, and I loved the unexpected bites of pitch black humor which caught me off guard every time. But its lack of compelling twists (or really any twists whatsoever) zaps the movie of some needed energy.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: It’s all very slick, ideal for a 30-second cigarette advert, if people still made those.
reviews.author: Robert Horton

reviews.text: This film doesn't give the audience much in regards to context and having something for us to remotely root for. This was a slow burn that never really paid off.
reviews.author: Justin Brown

reviews.text: There's nothing remotely erotic about this movie. It felt like the actors were just tired throughout the making of this.
reviews.author: Brandon Collins

reviews.text: Lyne tries to make an ode to jealousy as an aphrodisiac, and perhaps that makes sense to him, an 81-year-old man who found a gold mine in that kind of cinema seen today as fatuous, outdated and toxic. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Elsa Fernández-Santos

reviews.text: The movie is weirdly coy with its sex scenes (in that there are almost none of them) and it feels like there are chunks missing throughout obscuring the satisfaction of the inevitable escalation to full thriller.
reviews.author: Nathaniel Rogers

reviews.text: It's a very silly movie, but watchable in its blatant ludicrousness.
reviews.author: Jordan Ruimy

reviews.text: The biggest mystery is how this went so wrong, despite having all the right elements to succeed.
reviews.author: Nestor Bentancor

reviews.text: Doesn’t even work as a guilty pleasure. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text:
Superficial thriller with limited range.
[Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: The film's strong balance between seriousness and campiness, along with the sex appeal and star power of its leads, is enough to make up for most of what the film lacks.
reviews.author: Dan Bayer

reviews.text: Spiritually closer to Lyne's Unfaithful than his 80s and 90s Erotic Thrillers, Deep Water is best when it explores the tensions within Vic and Melinda's open marriage. Affleck's somnabulist performance plays nicely off of de Armas' tempestuous sexpot
reviews.author: Joe Lipsett

reviews.text: Considering Lyne's filmography, I was expecting something a little more passionate or even entertaining from "Deep Water"; both Affleck and de Armas deserved something less shallow. Full review in Spanish.
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: Deep Water never quite feels sexy enough for its lurid subject matter. Lyne may have been able to spin trash into art with his earlier efforts, but this film is a disappointingly shallow attempt at hearkening back to the glory days.
reviews.author: Brent Hankins

reviews.text: Its a shame, after all the work at building this strange tension, that the last 10 minutes are bungled in almost comical fashion.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: There are nuggets of good ideas here and Lyne directs the film with aplomb, but did it have to be this dull?
reviews.author: Trace Thurman

reviews.text: tricky territory that might have worked better and had a more profound and lasting effect had it been treated with more dramatic heft and less pulpy-erotic scheming
reviews.author: James Kendrick

reviews.text: Its too many snails.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: Deep Water doesn't quite represent the triumphant return of the star-studded erotic thriller... But it's a fun way to spend two hours and features two attractive leads messing with each other in a manner that sustains interest.
reviews.author: Dominic Corry

reviews.text: Honestly, reflecting on this movie for more than five minutes will make the whole thing melt in your hands, so it’s best not to consider it for too long.
reviews.author: Scaachi Koul

reviews.text: Were it better written there might at least be some drama to the whole affair (even if their sexual games feel far from lurid), but in its battle to feel promiscuous and dangerous it feels like neither.
reviews.author: Zosha Millman

reviews.text: This Southern-fried Freud-meets-Tennessee Williams tries so hard to be contemporary but is like a drug-and-sexed-up version of one of those 1950s housewife melodramas featuring a handsome ne-er-do-well arriving in town.
reviews.author: Lynn Venhaus

reviews.text: Believe it or not, its most outstanding achievement was making me laugh without even trying to be funny.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: With a few drinks under your belt on a Friday or Saturday night, this wonky flick from the director of Fatal Atrraction will do the trick just nicely/nastily.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: Deep Water is a star-studded throwback to the days when sexy thrillers about adults doing adult things didn't go straight to the small screen.
reviews.author: Margot Harrison

reviews.text: OK, it’s not Body Heat.  But it kept my motor running.
reviews.author: Rex Reed

reviews.text: "Deep Water" is a tepid version of what Lyne was once a master of doing.
reviews.author: Matthew Passantino

reviews.text: In Deep Water, the confused confluence of passion, jealousy and manliness are animating forces even among the so-very-civilized private schools and cocktail parties set.
reviews.author: David Bax

reviews.text: I didn't like this movie, mostly because I didn't believe this movie.
reviews.author: Tim Cogshell

reviews.text: Despite the credentials of those involved, it is a very flat film.
reviews.author: Lael Loewenstein

reviews.text: Even though there are moments throughout the film that defy believability, Deep Water is an enticing return for Lyne.
reviews.author: Chad Byrnes

reviews.text: Deep Water is a great example of what can happen when you let otherwise competent movie stars just go for it, for better or—and in this case it’s mostly “or”—worse.
reviews.author: Adam Mullins-Khatib

reviews.text: The cinematic equivalent of waiting for your bread to toast, only to realize hours later you forgot to plug in the damn thing.
reviews.author: Matt Pais

reviews.text: Adrian Lyne's best films intellectualise the juicy plotting of your average airport novel; Deep Water just feels like an average airport novel.
reviews.author: Simon Foster

reviews.text: Fortunately, Lyne does have Affleck and de Armas, and they certainly don't account for nothing, lifting the material far higher than their director ever could.
reviews.author: Jake Tropila

reviews.text: Deep Water is the worst film I've seen in a long time. The story never progresses and you keep waiting for the climax that never happens. The character's actions are never explained or given much depth.
reviews.author: Lupe Rodriguez Haas

reviews.text: Deep Water is far from the best movie youll see all year, but it has just enough gas in its tank to drive you to press play and keep you from exiting until the credits roll.
reviews.author: Jonathan Sim

reviews.text: Deep Water is an accomplished but essentially unremarkable entry in the Highsmith filmography.
reviews.author: Kelly Vance

reviews.text: In some ways, I’m happy to have even a simulacrum of a movie for grownups. But I’ve been waiting 20 years for the new Adrian Lyne to drop, as it were. This wasn’t worth the wait.
reviews.author: Max Weiss

reviews.text: A feeble, witless adaptation...Lyne and his screenwriters never stray from familiar tableaux... The actors portraying the emotionally sadomasochistic couple cant evince the merest spark of shambolic erotic energy between them.
reviews.author: Melissa Anderson

reviews.text: As Gothic, soapy, and tacky the story and execution, we want to see who wins.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: Lyne may not have recaptured his glory days here, but he has given us a robustly acted mystery thriller we can all sink our teeth into.
reviews.author: Linda Marric

reviews.text: This film, while satisfyingly glossy and sexy, is nevertheless too implausible and contrived to really generate much suspense.
reviews.author: Peg Aloi

reviews.text: What the ‘90s erotic thriller was to hardcore pornography, Deep Water is to the ‘90s erotic thriller: an echo of something way more stimulating.
reviews.author: Rich Juzwiak

reviews.text: Deep Water unravels quickly into a limpid and ultimately preposterous amble down a very predictable, intrigue-free path.
reviews.author: Hilary A White

reviews.text: Sleek and insinuating, this dark mystery holds the attention with its intense characters and offbeat situations, orchestrated expertly by veteran director Adrian Lyne.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: The only time (Affleck) seems to smile is looking at his snail farm. Anyone looking for a 2022 update of the Sad Ben Affleck meme will find a hard drives worth of material here.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: Nonsensical, but gleefully so...Deep Water isnt all that deep, but hey  splashing around in the shallow end can be fun too.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: I could have sworn that erotic thrillers were supposed to be erotic and/or thrilling.
reviews.author: Kevin Fallon

reviews.text: Deep Water is a movie for grown-ups. Not for prurient interests, mind, but for students of behaviour--of snails and other things.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: The master of the erotic thriller, Adrian Lyne, returns after 20 years; the master of self-aware acting, Ben Affleck, continues a stellar run. But something about this movie just leaves you feeling limp.
reviews.author: Adam Nayman

reviews.text: Despite its genre and two conventionally attractive leads, Hulu’s new movie leans more into weirdness than sexiness...
reviews.author: Jodi Walker

reviews.text: Committed performances by Ana de Armas and Ben Affleck aren't enough to save this frustrating and boring story, that's neither exciting or interesting. In general, a big letdown. Full review in Spanish
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: Cuban actress Ana de Armas's role as Melinda in "Deep Water" is certainly complex and dynamic, but, her character has me thinking maybe I should be a little more careful what I wish for.
reviews.author: Cristina Escobar

reviews.text: Sensational erotic adult thriller about rich people toying with infidelity. de Armas captives with a provocative performance. Grace Jenkins upstages de Armas with a song.
reviews.author: Victoria Alexander

reviews.text: Everything in Deep Water competent but a little bit dull
reviews.author: Carson Timar

reviews.text: It doesnt work, because the ambiguity of the characters is misapportioned.
reviews.author: CJ Sheu

reviews.text: Are we aroused in the same way as we enter the 2020s? Adrian Lyne's return with Deep Water looks to answer this question and while it doesn't entirely work, it does open a doorway long thought closed.
reviews.author: Tony Black

reviews.text: Deep Water seems determined to know nothing, and to bore us while doing so.
reviews.author: Noah Berlatsky

reviews.text: Deep Water has abandoned thought and logic for horny, unhinged vibes. It’s so much beautiful fun.
reviews.author: Alex Abad-Santos

reviews.text: There is a problem with a Patricia Highsmith adaptation of all things having a "don’t think too much and just vibe" approach given that her work is so proudly brainy. Still, I couldn’t help but be won over by this almost nostalgic offering.
reviews.author: Kayleigh Donaldson

reviews.text: Deep Water is a sweat-inducing psychological scheme that is constantly aiming to intrigue and titillate.
reviews.author: Natalia Keogan

reviews.text: Lyne keeps the pot simmering and simmering and then we look in the pot and it’s empty.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: It does, finally, get under the skin, if you can make it through the tepid sex and stretches of tedium. Melinda and Vics transgressiveness may not be explained, or believable, but it eventually becomes oddly compelling.
reviews.author: Sarah Cartland

reviews.text: It's a strange thing to call a Lyne movie tame, but by his standards, Deep Water is.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: Even if you're intrigued by the thought of a new erotic thriller in 2022, stay far away from "Deep Water."
reviews.author: Robert Levin

reviews.text: A shadowy role for Affleck, but not in a good way ... he can't seem to grasp character roles. This story also suffered from if you're trying to guess what's going on  and if you guess anywhere near correctly ... it wont be that great an experience.
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: Strange that a movie that's supposed to be an erotic thriller isn't very erotic or thrilling. Unexpected laughs keep this reasonably enjoyable despite its many flaws and no one has a scowling glare like Affleck.
reviews.author: Jim Laczkowski

reviews.text: Shallow Stream is a more appropriate title.
reviews.author: Cole Smithey

reviews.text: Deep Water seems to be a misbegotten vanity project greenlit in the first flush of a celebrity couple’s hots for one another, completed just as they break up, and thereafter politely ignored by everyone involved.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: It was hard for me to close the distance between myself and this movie, to get into it, simply because it felt ... mechanical. The seams show.
reviews.author: Linda Holmes

reviews.text: Deep Water's flaws and loose ends notwithstanding, there's a particular pleasure in watching Affleck and de Armas act out this dumpster fire of a marriage, no matter how implausible it becomes.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: A cheesy erotic thriller from a veteran of the genre, based on a Patricia Highsmith novel, may sound like movie gold, but the end result is eye-rollingly ridiculous.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: [A] tepid and frustratingly shallow thriller...
reviews.author: Andy Lea

reviews.text: "As a psycho-sexual whodunit, the perverse plot makes no sense whatever."
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: Hulu subscribers are in for here is a lukewarm R-rated affair that, while being highly concerned with attraction, is only occasionally fatal.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: Ben Affleck has more chemistry with a cup of Dunkin' Donuts in paparazzi pics than he has onscreen with Ana De Armas. What a shame this is the next of her films to come out after a delightful turn in "No Time to Die." At best it's a cacophony of mediocre.
reviews.author: Dana Han-Klein

reviews.text: In a world in which Gone Girl exists, this movie isn't very necessarily
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: This is an enjoyably dark peek into the desires and demands of an outwardly unhappy married couple that entertains with a deceptively light touch.
reviews.author: Rob Hunter

reviews.text: This was a solid attempt at something good but even with some good actors and some superb directing, the story doesnt hold together to make this a fulfilling watch.
reviews.author: Julian Lytle

reviews.text: All this is depicted, of course, with tactile beauty and visual restlessness; the human figures move in space, within decors that are sumptuous and simmer...  Polish and trashiness remain eager bedmates.
reviews.author: Ray Pride

reviews.text: This erotic thriller is short on thrills and eroticism.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: Waste of my time and their talent.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: Alas, a thriller is like flying across the ocean: You either get there or you don’t. Pilots get no credit for making it 90 percent of the way to Ireland, and this film sputters out of fuel in the final act.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: If there’s a point to it, Lyne is keeping it close to the vest. Perhaps it’s time for him to take a stab at something other than unholy matrimony.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: Deep Water doesn’t pan out. It doesn’t add up. Not in a fun way: in an unsatisfying way. The ingredients are largely there, but by even the standards of a genre that no one insists should make complete sense, the movie doesn’t really make sense.
reviews.author: K. Austin Collins

reviews.text: Deep Water aspires to be a boundary-pushing erotic thriller but is stuck treading water in the kiddie pool. Director Adrian Lyne, who used to be a bonafide closer in this genre, must have lost his “how to make it horny” handbook.
reviews.author: Tara Bennett

reviews.text: While the movie falls apart toward the end, the mystery -- and crackling central performances -- cruises along at a low boil much of the way.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: Deep Water is deeply dull.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: Through Lyne’s expertise as well as Affleck and de Armas’ gameness about their semi-transparency, the erotic thriller once again attains its highest aspiration by obliterating the concept of the guilty pleasure.
reviews.author: Charles Bramesco

reviews.text: Deep Water comes dressed up as an ‘80s-style erotic thriller, a genre that I, for one, would love to see revived. But it’s so tepid, so lacking in heat or even a pulse, that it’s about as sexy as a clogged artery.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: Deep Water might look slick, but feels both shallow and soulless.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: This one is bonkers. Top to bottom bonkers.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: t’s hard to believe that Adrian Lyne, responsible for huge box-office hits like the provocative thriller Fatal Attraction and the dodgy but watchable 9 ½ Weeks and Indecent Proposal, could make something quite so feeble as Deep Water.
reviews.author: Saskia Baron

reviews.text: Deep Water is a desperate attempt to provoke viewers instead of making them think.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: It’s steamy to be sure, and Armas carries it off with brazen bravado, but the film works only in wisps.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: It’s a welcome return for Lyne, who has lost none of his penchant for directly purveying the perverse tendencies of human nature railing against the rigidity of traditional relationships.
reviews.author: Nicholas Bell

reviews.text: ... watered down to fit a standard erotic thriller framework that lacks the necessary sizzle and ironic self-awareness, and never fulfills its twisty Hitchcockian ambitions.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: An erotic thriller that starts off intriguing, but sinks under its underdeveloped foundation.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Lyles

reviews.text: What should be a taut, gripping, suspense-laden thriller looks more like the husk of one despite all the major names in front of and behind the camera.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Harris

reviews.text: "Deep Water" is a tame attempt at a psychological thriller that never delves into the psychological, is short on thrills, and relies too much on the audience to fill in its own blanks.
reviews.author: Karen M. Peterson

reviews.text: The erotic part is very obvious. The thriller part is where the movie falls short.
reviews.author: Dan Murrell

reviews.text: Not a great book-to-screen adaptation, but the film is a slow burn thriller thats adequate enough to meet lowered expectations.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: Adrian Lyne misfire Deep Water wastes talents of Ben Affleck, Ana de Armas and author Patricia Highsmith.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: A vicious piece of work, a movie made by a filmmaker who is unafraid to see the primal, darker parts that beautiful people hide behind their gorgeous facades.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: Leaves things stuck in deep water.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: Ben Affleck sniffing his snails: that is what you are in for if you commit to watching Deep Water.
reviews.author: Dana Stevens

reviews.text: Deep Water makes it difficult for viewers to gravitate toward either lead character, but beyond that, the mystery is never compelling enough to care about.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: Deep Water plays like a sexy, macabre Whos Afraid of Virginia Woolf?, an intense dialogue between an unhappily married couple thats occasionally disrupted by outsiders.
reviews.author: Scott Tobias

reviews.text: Not the most elegant exploration of toxicity, but it's one that tackles the subject through refreshingly provocative intentions... Full Review in Spanish
reviews.author: Ricardo Gallegos

reviews.text: Adapted from the Patricia Highsmith novel by Zach Helm and Sam Levinson, the film is a hot mess almost from minute one. The editors of the film understood what a dog of a story they had on their hands, as the film is cut to within an inch of its life.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: Afflecks face lights up around gastropods in a way it doesnt around the humans in the movie.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: There are glimmers of the perversely fascinating murder mystery of the classic 1957 Patricia Highsmith novel, but this misguided update suffers from a lack of suspense, humor and undetectable sexual chemistry between stars Ben Affleck and Ana de Armas.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: While stylish and full of beautiful people, the pace is so off the characters seem far from believable.
reviews.author: Dulcie Pearce

reviews.text: De Armas was practically designed in a lab to make movies like this: shes just pure, smoldering temptation, careening into open arms wherever she finds them.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: Lacks suspense and, increasingly, credibility as it grunts and strains its way towards an overwrought ending.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: The performers could hardly interact more damply if they were exchanging dialogue on Zoom from different continents.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: Hear me out, but is Vic a giant metaphor for American foreign policy?
reviews.author: Rohan Naahar

reviews.text: Confounding and almost completely devoid of chemistry between its leads.
reviews.author: Emily Zemler

reviews.text: The movie we witness feels like the aftermath in a violent marital kitchen spat, with china and glassware weaponized in anger, and cutting shards of what Deep Water could have been everywhere.
reviews.author: Radheyan Simonpillai

reviews.text: This movie struck me as a compelling argument against early retirement.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: So much for the long wait after 20 years. I figured Adrian Lynes return to feature filmmaking would bring back the long-stale erotic-thriller genre to its former glory. Too bad Deep Water isnt one of them.
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: Levinson and Helm feed the talented cast horrendous dialogue, none worse than a car-set sequence that finds Letts talking to himself like he's Lennie from Of Mice and Men.
reviews.author: Edwin Arnaudin

reviews.text: There is a sleaziness to the characters that make them both repulsive and fascinating.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: If Deep Water is cynical about the capacity for murder, it is also and equally scathing about the underlying drives, desires, and needs of love and marriage.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Its less than 2 hours long but definitely feels longer and the mind games are neither tense nor chilling. Adrian Lyne seems to have lost his touch in terms of creating a sexy, mysterious atmosphere as he did with his previous films.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: Deep Water feels like titillation dressed up as drama. Both actors bring lots of conviction, but the plot holes keep appearing, to remind us that everything is being pushed too hard.
reviews.author: Paul Byrnes

reviews.text: A wickedly funny potboiler about sex, gossip and hypocrisy that Mr. Lyne has transplanted from the suburban Northeast to New Orleans, a city that sweats menace despite the films chilly blue cinematography and coldly erotic score
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: Deep Water is an Aesop Tale for grown-ups minus the moral. Lyne is in the business of fantasy. The biggest fantasy Lyne sells in Deep Water is of a world where no available moment to have sex is wasted.
reviews.author: Thom Ernst

reviews.text: Despite a strong cast, Deep Water never quite comes together. Its a recipe with all the right ingredients but an entirely misguided execution. Hardly more than a pale shade of erotic thrillers past, Deep Water is nothing but an empty glass.
reviews.author: Aly Caviness

reviews.text: Deep Water is proof that it's not enough to have good-looking people in a stylish-looking film. It has a basic mystery that's not very suspenseful, in addition to monotonous mind games played by the central married couple.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: A fairly superficial take on the novel, more characteristic of Lyne than Highsmith; but fans of the author in particular will find it intriguing, even if the characters motivations remain more cryptic than compelling.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: A mix of high-class prestige drama and trashy smut, is the sweet spot that Deep Water nails that other similar films drown trying to emulate.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: Deep Water, despite an all-star team behind it, barely makes a splash. Although it is being billed as an erotic thriller, it’s tedious and clunky. Trips to the supermarket are more exciting.
reviews.author: Mark Kennedy

reviews.text: Based on a novel by Patricia Highsmith and directed by Adrian Lyne (Fatal Attraction), Deep Water savors the thrills of sadistic foreplay.
reviews.author: Bennett Campbell Ferguson

reviews.text: It is at best moderately successful. But its also a movie that seems not to care what you think of it.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: Something went wrong here – it feels like the final cut of the film is either the victim of duff scripting choices, or made equally duff attempts to fix them.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: a cold plunge into shallow erotic thriller territory.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: Occasional moments are outright camp. Even these feel halfhearted, the movie forever at odds with itself: flippant but morose, nervously post-#MeToo but also made more ethically grubby than the story ever was in 1957.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: Still waters run turgid in this limp psycho-sexual thriller starring Ben Affleck and Ana de Armas as a wealthy couple who get off in very twisted ways.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: A candidate for one of the worst films of 2022.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: Know who are cuckolding. If he looks like Ben Affleck, turn and run away.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: It may be sold as hot, but "Deep Water" goes as cold as a snail's trail.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: I can see some viewers checking out as the narrative twists down a road of preposterous paths, but fans of the genre should buckle up for one of the early year's best crowdpleasers.
reviews.author: Matt Conway

reviews.text: The movie appears chopped into misaligned chunks and dangling loose ends, its scenes spat out as randomly as bingo balls.
reviews.author: Jeannette Catsoulis

reviews.text: Watching Deep Water is equivalent to driving past a bad car accident.  You don't want to look but you simply cant turn away.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: We've moved away from adult thrillers in recent years, so it's great to have Lyne back with a film that isn't afraid to show the messy side of love and people.
reviews.author: Natasha Alvar

reviews.text: Adrian Lyne, in his first film in twenty years, seems unable to tease out the tension from the love-hate  story, sexual or otherwise.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: "Deep Water" could be, maybe should be, a touch trashier, but its wackadoodle enough that I was shamefully gleeful when one character met their end.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: For a stylish thriller to work, it needs to be at least a little bit stylish and offer an occasional thrill. “Deep Water” does neither.
reviews.author: Mark Feeney

reviews.text: Lyne has always gone the extra step, and “Deep Water” shows that he hasn’t lost his touch.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: Notably and refreshingly, Lyne largely seems to have purged himself of the moralistic streak that’s often marred his work; for the first time in a long time, he’s enjoying his characters’ awfulness rather than damning them for it.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: Deep Water isn't really thrilling or erotic, but it accomplishes a kind of diagonal camp sincerity, plummeting its glamorous characters into ever-tawdrier situations.
reviews.author: Darren Franich

reviews.text: Deep Water has its moments, but it simmers when it should sizzle. For numerous reasons, things stay stuck closer to neutral than high gear, which leaves you wanting more.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: Gonna let you know right up front: Deep Water is not for me. But its not for you either, and its not for anyone who likes a well-written, well-directed, and well-cast motion picture.
reviews.author: Don Kaye

reviews.text: The problem with Deep Water is its slow-burning plot revelations are just too repetitive and full of narrative nonsense as to emphasize this film’s complete lack of credibility.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: The co-stars sizzled in real life, and their chemistry oozes through the screen. But everything else about this mess of an erotic thriller is a baffling tease.
reviews.author: Laura Bradley

reviews.text: Affleck seems bored...meanwhile, Ana de Armas goes over the top as his cheating wife in a thriller that tries but fails to be sexy.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: For the sake of moral complicity, Lyne injects an amorality that takes the steam out of this steamy potboiler.
reviews.author: Neil Morris

reviews.text: Not unentertaining, featuring as it does some choice moments of high camp, among them a dinner scene where Affleck implicitly threatens someone with his snail collection.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: Doesnt invoke the beads of sweat that the genres best can manage, but its a pleasurably trashy reminder of the flashy fun that Lyne and his many imitators once regularly brought to the screen.
reviews.author: Alonso Duralde

reviews.text: If you can get past some of the silly choices that factor into the plot to the multitude of supporting characters and subplots that go nowhere, Deep Water still manages to tell an evocative murder mystery with a less than surprising whodunit at its core.
reviews.author: Alex Maidy

reviews.text: The "is he or isn't he?" mystery plays out for a while, until we are given a definitive answer. What we're left with instead is "will she care?" And that's where the movie gets interesting.
reviews.author: Jordan Hoffman

reviews.text: A slog of a film that ends up with an equally huh?? ending, Deep Water is a film that anyone involved will hope to forget as quickly as anyone who watches it.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: Ben Affleck fumes as Ana de Armas cavorts in a tawdry thriller that's borderline laughable. Deep Water is loaded with nudity, kinky romps, and murder. The eye candy does not sustain a failed attempt at psychological machinations.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: It shepherds a sadly ailing cinematic tradition forward with the same luminous style, a welcome sensuality, and in an era in which pornography is more widely available than ever before, an astute bit of camp.
reviews.author: Todd Gilchrist

reviews.text: A movie as cold and inert as Vic's pet snails.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: "Deep Water" is a very silly movie that has elements of campy B-movie mediocrity.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: Not only does this delirious movie find [director Adrian Lyne] swan-diving back into the same fetid lap pool of envy, lust, and psychosexual control where he used to swim laps every morning, it finds that he’s basically got an entire lane to himself.
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: The audience is left hung out to dry.
reviews.author: Phil Villarreal

reviews.text: There’s nothing wrong with a thriller leaving some loose ends. But “Deep Water” trips over them too often.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: Deep Water has satirical tendencies, yet the banal dialogue and clunky/confusing plot means we laugh at it, not with it.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: A robust, well-acted thriller that lands most of its major twists gracefully; for that, all lesser sins can be forgiven.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: Lyne draws out the elements of the story that arent laid out in the text, the darker, far more subversive themes that lie below the surface in this tale of an unconventional marriage.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: True to Lyne’s form, Deep Water is a slick, entertaining cod-psychological thriller, just classy enough to be aspirational, and just seedy enough to satisfy a craving for cinematic junk food.
reviews.author: Oli Welsh

reviews.text: In 2022, films of this ilk are so rare, that I can almost forgive Deep Water's faults just for reminding me that these sorts of stories can be told onscreen.
reviews.author: Matt Singer

reviews.text: This erotic thriller is the kind of flick that will make you ache for the days when you could hang out in the theater lobby afterwards and talk it out.
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: The knobs are turned as tight as can be and emotions are pushed to the edge, in the sexy, seductive, and downright wild Deep Water.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: Manages to drain all the subtlety and psychological complexity from Highsmith’s story of marital warfare, transgression and obsession.
reviews.author: David Rooney

reviews.text: Deep Water is extremely uncomfortable & frustrating to watch. It's impossible to like either of the lead characters, which makes it hard to connect to the film as a whole. Final 15 mins are great -- just takes too long to get there.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: Melinda is cold as ice and wholly unlikable  and thus is a fascinating performance to see from Ana de Armas.
reviews.author: Eric Eisenberg

reviews.text: The resolution is a bit too convenient for the complexities the film had established. A disappointing ending could ruin the whole film, but the Van Allens' relationship is fascinating enough to watch, regardless.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: Deep Water is billed as an erotic thriller, but it builds up little urgency because its stakes are never clear.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: Lyne’s a talented enough director to keep us invested, even in the film’s lunatic last third.
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

reviews.text: Deep Water is finally being let out of its own misery...
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: Ben Affleck is the alpha cuck in the glorious return of the mid-budget adult sex thriller.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: The film took so long to come out, Affleck and de Armas dated, broke up and have already moved on to other relationships. Audiences should consider doing the same.
reviews.author: Catherine Springer

reviews.text: Deep Water gets bogged down by familiar and pedantic elements of an erotic thriller that feels 65 years old.
reviews.author: Emily Wheeler

reviews.text: I'm not sure if Deep Water is art or trash. I just know that it's immensely entertaining, and people are going to greatly enjoy debating whether it's art or trash.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: More eviscerating character-driven psychodrama than smutty erotic thriller, its a tantalizing, scintillating and inspired entry in the sub-genre.
reviews.author: Courtney Howard

reviews.text: The end result isn't very compelling. Deep Water﻿ is a dull and bland thriller held back by a weak script that even Affleck and de Armas can't save.
reviews.author: Chris Agar

reviews.text: In 2022 its a true gift seeing a film so unafraid of being as lurid, provocative, and unabashedly horny as Deep Water.
reviews.author: Mitchell Beaupre

reviews.text: While it struggles to be erotic or even a thriller, our two leads carry this bland film to a decent martial drama.
reviews.author: EJ Moreno

reviews.text: Deep Water falters as a romantic thriller, no thanks to whiplash editing and a lack of chemistry between its two stars.
reviews.author: Collier Jennings

reviews.text: For a director who has given the world erotic thrillers like Fatal Attraction, Jacobs Ladder, and Indecent Proposal, Deep Water lacked the passion and desire that Lyne has always been so capable of crafting on screen.
reviews.author: Maggie Lovitt

reviews.text: Deep Water is about as exciting as Vic and Melinda's on-the-rocks relationship. There's no spark; there's no thrill. Like their marriage, the film just goes through the motions.
reviews.author: Matt Rodriguez

reviews.text: The dynamic between Ana De Armas and Ben Affleck is fascinating: not ridiculous enough to be camp, but not far off.
reviews.author: Sophie Monks Kaufman

reviews.text: Deep Water is a misfire of an erotic thriller.
reviews.author: Jeff Nelson

reviews.text: Deep Water is a genuine instance where the old adage "They don't make 'em like they used to" applies all too well.
reviews.author: Josh Spiegel

reviews.text: After a dangerous, even personal, first half, Deep Water becomes crude in all the wrong ways.
reviews.author: Chuck Bowen

reviews.text: A joy from start to finish.
reviews.author: Elena Lazic

reviews.text: While some may be upset that Deep Water isn't the erotic thriller its provocative trailers teased, I personally found it more rewarding: a satire of toxic masculinity, disguised as a delightfully trashy genre piece.
reviews.author: Alistair Ryder

reviews.text: What could have been an intriguing marital study, exploring the hidden depths of a doomed relationship like Gone Girl, instead falls flat - feeling surprisingly devoid of both lust and intrigue.
reviews.author: Nicola Austin

reviews.text: A nice return for Lyne, who plays to his strengths with the endeavor, making a sinister and sexual picture, and one that does well with Affleck and de Armas, who share terrific chemistry.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: Success mostly hangs on Ben Affleck and Ana de Armas believably psychologically going to war with one another, which they do with numerous stares and heated body language
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Lyne’s return to the sweat-soaked stage trades bodice-ripping intrigue for repetitive boredom and psychosexual mind games with a straightforward descent into semi-madness.
reviews.author: Clint Worthington

reviews.text: Deep Water is an intriguing thriller which is a throwback to the type of film Hollywood used to frequently turn-out in the '80s and '90s. If youre in the mood for an expertly produced retro domestic thriller then Deep Water is the movie for you.
reviews.author: Niall Browne

reviews.text: A movie so outdated in its view of women and relationships, and so outlandishly pervy and reductive, they should have called it Male Gaze.
reviews.author: Johanna Schneller

reviews.text: Adrian Lynes toothless erotic thriller starring Ben Affleck and Ana De Armas has few thrills and less chemistry. A tepid, shallow shame.
reviews.author: Adam Solomons

reviews.text: Whatever catharsis is to be found in the ritualistic enactment of one’s worst impulses, it’s in the very foundations of Ben Affleck and Ana de Armas’s performances in the erotic (or not so erotic) thriller Deep Water.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: Despite his erotic thriller credentials, Lyne makes a tepid return to the director’s chair with a rather basic adaptation of an intriguing marital character study that Affleck struggles to enliven.
reviews.author: Hanna Flint

reviews.text: Deep Water presents itself as a safe project for Lyne to return to cinema. But despite the appeal of Affleck and de Armas, it is one that is poorly executed.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: What a thrill it is to see this sort of film  for and about adults, unafraid to be sexually explicit and morally opaque  in a day where so many films taste like watered-down juice.
reviews.author: Steph Green

reviews.text: Compared to Lynes earlier work, Deep Water is ragged; its not got the same zeitgeist-tapping polish of Fatal Attraction. But theres something enjoyably trashy about it that fans of erotic thrillers, and of Highsmiths novels, will get a kick out of.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: De Armas behaves as if she’s in some saucy cologne commercial, and Affleck appears to have necked a hundredweight of Percocet before the cameras rolled.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: Deep Water is a tense and involving thriller that adapts Highsmiths intense storytelling to the modern world with some style
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: It's a shame that a film that purports to be an erotic thriller is neither sexy nor tense.
reviews.author: Gabriella Geisinger

reviews.text: Especially shocking is Lynes failure to capture onscreen any of the supposed chemistry that took place off-screen. Erotic thrillers used to be the director's forte, but here the sex scenes between Affleck and De Armas feel entirely mannered.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: Continually comical in a way that feels at first intentional if chaotic, then camp, then baffling, the film fumbles its potential scene after scene.
reviews.author: Amanda Jane Robinson

reviews.text: In the end, both Vic and Melinda come across as so unlikeable that it's difficult to care about what happens to either of them.
reviews.author: Terry Staunton

synopsis: Based on the celebrated novel by famed mystery writer Patricia Highsmith (The Talented Mr. Ripley), "Deep Water" takes us inside the marriage of picture-perfect Vic (Ben Affleck) and Melinda (Ana de Armas) Van Allen to discover the dangerous mind games they play and what happens to the people that get caught up in them.
